solved_in: The first relation is the free part (on shell the Proca Lagrangian is a total derivative); the second (Feynman-Hellmann) reproduces the trace-anomaly gluon condensate to $10^{-16}$; SU(2): $d_{\mathrm{adj}} = 3$, $C_{\mathrm{adj}} = 2$, $T_{\mathrm{F}}N_{\mathrm{f}} = 3$; U(1)$_Y$: $d_{\mathrm{adj}} = 1$, $C_{\mathrm{adj}} = 0$, $\frac52T_{\mathrm{F}}N_{\mathrm{f}} \to \frac{25}{2}$; no scalar term (ESTIMATE).

title: The electroweak condensates of a hot plasma
solved_in: Below $m_{\mathrm{W}}$ the order-$\alpha_{\mathrm{G}}$ part is multiplied by the thermal suppression of a massive vector (ESTIMATE); at the freeze-out the $W$ condensate is $-5.0\times10^{11}$ GeV$^4$, almost all from the interaction part.

solved_in: Iterated with the masses until self-consistency (the loop gain is at most $1.1\times10^{-33}$, so one step suffices); the block moves by at most $\Delta\ln f = 1.1\times10^{-34}$ (at the freeze-out).
